_comment: THE DECLARED RELEASE CHANNELS — every MOVING image label the platform publishes or reserves,
in ONE place (policy `declared-release-channels`; manual Doc/Architecture/ReleaseEditions).
A channel label is a TAG that moves (`3-latest`, `3-mac`, `3-enterprise`, `main`), never a
version: versions stay plain SemVer and carry no channel word (policy
`platform-semver-versioning`). A label names WHICH build an edition currently offers; a
deployment still runs a resolved VERSION (a pointer is a seed, never a running pin).
WHO READS THIS FILE, and the one rule each reader keeps:
* retention (lock-pinned-digests.py, and any pruner) — every label matching an entry below is
PROTECTED: the tag is never deleted, nor the manifest it names at the moment of the sweep. A
label is moving, so it is never LOCKED to a digest (that would pin bytes the label has
left); it is excluded by NAME. Removing an entry is the ONLY way to release a label.
`declared` entries are protected too, so a label is safe before its writer ships.
* writers (main-cd.yml, release.yml) — a workflow may write a moving label only if an entry
here names that workflow as its writer and is `written`.
* `release-channels.py check .` (every pull request) — the file is well formed, every
writer exists, the line pointers agree with platform-version.py, and lock-pinned-digests.py
classifies every label as floating.
`status`: written  — a writer moves it today.
declared — reserved and protected; no writer yet (`writer.state` says what is owed).
retired  — no writer moves it any more; still protected while a consumer may resolve it.
`notation`: any | legacy — `legacy` labels are written only for a pre-SemVer set (`3.0.0-ci.<n>`).

placeholders.patch: the version's patch — the legacy notation's line patch, e.g. 0 in 3.0.0-ci.8080
